name: t3code
description: Your own T3 Code server: agents read, start, message and stop T3 threads and projects. One connection per T3 server, signed in with a T3 pairing code.

scopeNotes.note: Full access in T3: agents can also add and change projects, T3's settings and source control, and T3's browser preview runs in your browser profile with its saved logins. If they don't need that, reconnect and pick a lower level.

Full access in T3: agents can also add and change projects, T3's settings and source control, and T3's browser preview runs in your browser profile with its saved logins. If they don't need that, reconnect and pick a lower level.
Agents can read, start, message and stop T3 threads. T3's browser preview runs in your browser profile on that computer, with its saved logins.
Read only in T3: agents can read projects and threads, nothing more.

setup.title: Enter your T3 Code server's address
setup.body: The address you open T3 Code at, such as `http://100.101.102.103:3773` on Tailscale or `http://127.0.0.1:3773` on this computer. xaq adds `/mcp`. Plain http is accepted only on this computer and your private network (Tailscale's 100.x addresses, 10.x, 172.16 to 172.31, 192.168.x); anywhere else T3 has to be on https. Each T3 server is its own connection, named after its address unless you name it.

setup.title: Have a T3 pairing code ready
setup.body: T3's approval page asks for a one-time pairing code. Make one in T3 Code under Settings → Connections, or run `t3 auth pairing create` on the computer T3 runs on. When `t3 serve` starts it prints one too: the Token line, which is also the part after `#token=` in its Pairing URL. A code works once and expires soon after it's made, so get it just before you connect.

setup.title: In T3, choose what agents may do
setup.body: T3 asks how much to allow. Pick the least your agents need. Read only: they read projects and threads. Supervised (Limited on older T3 versions): they can also start, message and stop threads, and those threads still ask before commands and file changes. The levels above it let threads run commands and edit files without asking, and Full access also lets agents add and change projects, T3's settings and source control. We recommend Supervised (or Limited) unless an agent needs more. Depending on the level, agents can also use T3's browser preview, which runs in your browser profile on that computer with its saved logins: they can browse websites as you. xaq shows what T3 granted, and still asks you before risky actions such as deleting a project, running JavaScript in a page or uploading files to one, at the access level you choose next.

setup.title: Reconnect every 30 days
setup.body: A T3 sign-in lasts 30 days and T3 can't renew it. xaq reminds you 7 days and 1 day before, in the console and through your webhooks and listener. Reconnect takes a new pairing code and keeps this connection's name, agents and access. If it does expire, agents get a message asking you to reconnect, not a failure in the middle of a task.
